{{alias}}( order, vect, M, N, K, A, LDA, TAU, WORK, LWORK )
    Generates one of the real orthogonal matrices `Q` or `P**T` determined
    by `DGEBRD` when reducing a real matrix `A` to bidiagonal form:
    `A = Q * B * P**T`.

    `Q` and `P**T` are defined as products of elementary reflectors `H(i)`
    or `G(i)` respectively.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    The function mutates `A` and `WORK`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string
        Storage layout. Must be either 'row-major' or 'column-major'.

    vect: string
        Specifies whether the matrix `Q` or the matrix `P**T` is returned in
        `A`. Must be either 'Q' or 'P'.

    M: integer
        Number of rows of `Q` or `P**T`.

    N: integer
        Number of columns of `Q` or `P**T`.

        If `vect` is 'Q', `N` must be greater than or equal to `min(M,K)` and
        smaller than or equal to `M`. If `vect` is 'P', `N` must be greater
        than or equal to `M`, and `M` must be greater than or equal to
        `min(N,K)`.

    K: integer
        If `vect` is 'Q', the number of columns in the original `M-by-K`
        matrix reduced by `DGEBRD`. If `vect` is 'P', the number of rows in
        the original `K-by-N` matrix reduced by `DGEBRD`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output matrix. On entry, `A` contains the vectors which define
        the elementary reflectors, as returned by `DGEBRD`. On exit, `A` is
        overwritten by the `M-by-N` matrix `Q` or `P**T`.

    LDA: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A` (a.k.a., leading dimension of the
        matrix `A`). Must be at least `max(1,M)` when `order` is
        `'column-major'` and at least `max(1,N)` when `order` is `'row-major'`.

    TAU: Float64Array
        Scalar factors of the elementary reflectors. Must have length
        `min(M,K)` if `vect` is 'Q' and length `min(N,K)` if `vect` is 'P'.

    WORK: Float64Array
        Workspace array.

    LWORK: integer
        Dimension of the array `WORK`. Must be at least `max(1,min(M,N))`,
        unless equal to `-1`, in which case a workspace query is performed and
        the optimal size of `WORK` is returned in `WORK[0]`.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. A status code of `0` indicates success.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}([ 1,0,0,-1,-2,0 ]);
    > var TAU = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1, 1 ] );
    > var WORK = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 10 );
    > {{alias}}( 'column-major', 'P', 2, 3, 2, A, 2, TAU, WORK, 10 )
    0
    > A
    <Float64Array>[ 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0 ]
    > WORK[ 0 ]
    64


{{alias}}.ndarray(vect,M,N,K,A,sA1,sA2,oA,TAU,sTAU,oTAU, WORK,sWORK,oWORK,LWORK)
    Generates one of the real orthogonal matrices `Q` or `P**T` determined
    by `DGEBRD` when reducing a real matrix `A` to bidiagonal form using
    alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing semantics based on starting
    indices.

    The function mutates `A` and `WORK`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    vect: string
        Specifies whether the matrix `Q` or the matrix `P**T` is returned in
        `A`. Must be either 'Q' or 'P'.

    M: integer
        Number of rows of `Q` or `P**T`.

    N: integer
        Number of columns of `Q` or `P**T`.

        If `vect` is 'Q', `N` must be greater than or equal to `min(M,K)` and
        smaller than or equal to `M`. If `vect` is 'P', `N` must be greater
        than or equal to `M`, and `M` must be greater than or equal to
        `min(N,K)`.

    K: integer
        If `vect` is 'Q', the number of columns in the original `M-by-K`
        matrix reduced by `DGEBRD`. If `vect` is 'P', the number of rows in
        the original `K-by-N` matrix reduced by `DGEBRD`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output matrix. On entry, `A` contains the vectors which define
        the elementary reflectors, as returned by `DGEBRD`. On exit, `A` is
        overwritten by the `M-by-N` matrix `Q` or `P**T`.

    sA1: integer
        Stride length for the first dimension of `A`.

    sA2: integer
        Stride length for the second dimension of `A`.

    oA: integer
        Starting index for `A`.

    TAU: Float64Array
        Scalar factors of the elementary reflectors. Must have length
        `min(M,K)` if `vect` is 'Q' and length `min(N,K)` if `vect` is 'P'.

    sTAU: integer
        Stride length for `TAU`.

    oTAU: integer
        Starting index for `TAU`.

    WORK: Float64Array
        Workspace array.

    sWORK: integer
        Stride length for `WORK`.

    oWORK: integer
        Starting index for `WORK`.

    LWORK: integer
        Dimension of the array `WORK`. Must be at least `max(1,min(M,N))`,
        unless equal to `-1`, in which case a workspace query is performed and
        the optimal size of `WORK` is returned in `WORK[0]`.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. A status code of `0` indicates success.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}([ 1,0,0,-1,-2,0 ]);
    > var TAU = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1, 1 ] );
    > var WORK = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 10 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( `P`, 2, 3, 2, A, 1, 2, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, 10 )
    0
    > A
    <Float64Array>[ 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0 ]
    > WORK[ 0 ]
    64

    See Also
    --------
